messages:
incidents-bot: PAGER ALERT — High error-rate on serving runtime in prod-us-west-2. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs -> container crashloops -> node flaps. Autoscaler triggered rapid scale-up then immediate scale-down (snapback). Potential customer impact on several Dedicated pools. Incident channel opened. @sre-oncall please triage. :rotating_light:
sre-oncall: On it. I'm grabbing logs and tracing the autoscaler actions. Repro: within last 7m saw 3x scale-up events followed by 2x scale-downs. Will post metrics and node list shortly.
aj: I grabbed kube events and logs from the serving pods. Seeing these patterns: kernel OOM kills inside container, then kube restarts container -> liveness probes fail -> pod marked NotReady -> node becomes unschedulable briefly then the autoscaler spins up new nodes.

maria: Quick mitigation proposals: 1) Pause autoscaler for the affected pool to stop oscillation (kubectl annotate or patch autoscaler). 2) Drain the worst nodes and cordon to avoid further pods landing on hot nodes. 3) Roll back to lower-concurrency/quantized model variant for the hot routes to reduce memory footprint.

kevin: Agree with pause. On metrics: tail token latency spikes with 95th jumping to 4s, memory per-pod trending from 48GB -> 61GB before OOM. I'm seeing GPU mem fragmentation in the stack traces. Sending pointer to trace: https://internal.metrics.prod/redwood/trace/abc123

jess: Customer impact: two Dedicated customers reported elevated error rates via support. We're seeing some 5xxs from hosted API too on specific shards (us-west-2a). Filing incident impact notice to the escalations queue.

infra-bot: Autoscaler events snapshot (recent): 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z scale up pool-serving-usw2 from 8 -> 16 (demand spike)
2026-03-15T14:03:07Z scale down pool-serving-usw2 from 16 -> 10 (threshold)
2026-03-15T14:04:52Z scale up pool-serving-usw2 from 10 -> 18 (new influx)
2026-03-15T14:05:40Z scale down pool-serving-usw2 from 18 -> 9 (snapback)
```

ops: I'm executing the pause: patching the HorizontalPodAutoscaler to paused=true for pool-serving-usw2. Command: `kubectl patch hpa pool-serving-usw2 -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleDown":null}}}'` — I'm using conservative patch to stop downward scaling first.

sre-oncall: Also starting controlled drains on nodes with repeated OOMs: `kubectl drain node/gpu-node-27 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — doing one at a time. Notifying workload owners.

aj: Logs (excerpt): 
```
[E 14:03:05] runtime: CUDA out of memory allocating 134217728 bytes
[E 14:03:05] trace: kv-cache growth + quant layers pinned
[Restart] liveness probe failed after 5 retries
```

maria: To reduce memory pressure now: 1) ship a quick config to scale per-pod max-concurrency to 1 for the hot model route, 2) switch to 16-bit quantized variant (model-q16) for the next rollout, 3) enable prefix KV cache eviction. I can push the per-route config in the console, need sign-off.

kevin: Please do the per-route concurrency reduction first — that's low-risk. I'll stage the quantized variant as fallback and only route 20% initially.

jess: Support message drafted: "We're investigating elevated errors in us-west-2. Some customers may experience intermittent 5xx on model endpoints. Mitigation in progress; we'll update in 30 minutes." Sending now.

infra-bot: Noting node-level events: gpu-node-27, gpu-node-31 reported repeated GPU driver resets (nvidia-driver 535.86) around OOMs. Possible interplay between driver and CUDA allocator leading to fragmentation.

ops: After pause, autoscaler ceased downward moves. New pods scheduled onto freshly provisioned nodes with more headroom. Early signs: error rate started to decline. Will monitor for 10m window.

sre-oncall: Rolling summary for handoff: paused autoscaler for pool-serving-usw2, drained nodes 27 & 31, reduced route concurrency to 1 for hot route, staged model-q16 as canary 20%. Observed 40% reduction in OOM frequency since actions. Still watching for node flaps. @next-oncall you are up for the next 60m.

next-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll take over monitoring and coordinate re-enabling autoscaler once stable for 30m. If OOMs reappear, escalate to infra team for driver downgrade or kernel tunables.

aj: Follow-up notes for postmortem: suspected root causes: 1) workload transient demand spike with long context leading to unexpected KV cache growth, 2) GPU memory fragmentation + driver resets exacerbating OOMs, 3) aggressive autoscaler settings (short cooldowns) causing snapback oscillation and crashloops.

maria: I'll open an action ticket: tune autoscaler cooldowns, add memory headroom heuristics, improve per-model memory caps, and add a runbook for immediate pause + drain.

jess: Customer comms: sent update. Will post final status once next-oncall confirms stable for 30m.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigation in progress — partial recovery observed. Severity: P2 (customer impact limited to a few Dedicated pools). Continue monitoring.

ops: tagging for infra: @infra-team please look at driver reset correlation when you can.

infra-team (react): :eyes: will investigate driver logs and kernel messages.

sre-oncall: Thanks all. Save logs and attach to the incident ticket. We'll follow-up with a brief postmortem with timeline and action items.

next-oncall: Taking point. I'll run 30m steady-state check and then re-enable autoscaler with increased downscale stabilization window if good.

maria: Adding note — consider enabling VM hot-swap fallback (route to CPU fallback variant) for future incidents to reduce crashblast.

jess: Noted for comms template.

incidents-bot: AUTO-CLOSE WARNING: channel will remain open until oncall resolves. Use /incident close when done.
